This pattern was found by scanning the card's transaction history for bursts of similar transactions. The exposure from this pattern is $1,200.20. The fraud affects cardholders whose cards are used in this manner. The pattern does not fit any known typology and was identified by an agent through the analysis of transaction data.

sar.narrative: Customer C04285, holder of card C04285-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-18 14:43 and 2016-12-18 14:52, 3 transaction(s) totalling $1,200.20 were made on the card online from device profile 'Windows | Windows 10 | edge 17.0 | 1920x1079': $400.05 (3553899, 2016-12-18 14:43), $400.08 (3553904, 2016-12-18 14:44), $400.07 (3553923, 2016-12-18 14:52). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transactions and still holds the card. The activity is suspicious because: 3 online purchases within 9 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($400.05, $400.08, $400.07; total $1,200.20). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-4169, CC-4086, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.

stop_reason: The requested verification settled it: the cardholder denied the activity, raising the probability to 0.97. Further graph steps would not change the actions (policy 6).
